column1: # Every campaign the outcome funnel counts, one per line (#605).
# Columns (tab-separated, exactly five, TABS not spaces):
#   campaign    the label spike/outcome-funnel.tsv groups by. A LABEL, not a path:
#               two of this project's filings come from a 2026-09-04 measurement that
#               left no directory behind, and a column that had to be a directory
#               could not carry them at all.
#   date        when the campaign ran. For the dogfood runs it is the date in the
#               directory's name; for the older records it is the day the record was
#               first committed (`git log --diff-filter=A`), which is the only date
#               those directories carry. `summary --since` reads this column.
#   coverage    full         every target this campaign met has a row
#               filings-only only the targets whose findings were filed upstream.
#                            The reach counts in `summary` are taken over `full`
#                            campaigns alone, because a count over a set that was
#                            never fully entered is not a measurement.
#   candidates  how many candidates the campaign screened before fixing its slate, as
#               the campaign's own record states, or - where it kept no such count.
#               One number rather than a row per candidate: the candidate tables are
#               structured differently per run and are easy to count two ways (a
#               straightforward count of 2026-09-16-userview-3's tables gives 63 where
#               the run's own record says 41, because the rule-10 screen repeats
#   evidence    a path in this repository that must exist.
